items.title: 'Destabilising': Chinese ballistic missile test in Pacific prompts government concerns
items.description: China has test-fired a long-range missile with a dummy warhead in the Pacific Ocean, prompting concerns from the Australian government.

items.title: NSW government announces review into boy's death amid cannibalism probe
items.description: Cannibalism will form part of an investigation into the death of a four-year-old boy on the NSW Central Coast, with an independent review to take place by the Department of Communities and Justice.

items.title: 'Disappointing': Prince Harry and King's awkward stand-off over palace
items.description: The strained relationship between Prince Harry and his father, King Charles III, has been laid bare once again, after an awkward stand-off over accommodation at Buckingham Palace.

items.title: Trump says he asked FIFA to review US striker's World Cup red card
items.description: Football's European governing body blasts the decision to suspend a US striker's World Cup red-card ban, saying FIFA had "crossed a red line" after US President Donald Trump personally intervened in the case.

items.title: Socceroos winger says One Nation monoculture debate 'bulls***'
items.description: The Socceroos star says anyone "trying to divide" the community is "probably not Australian themselves".

items.title: 'Terrifying' roadside assistance ordeal sparks national change
items.description: A woman's campaign for change after her own frightening experience being broken down outside Canberra will see NRMA roadside assistance contractors required to provide a code to customers to verify their identity.

items.title: Second Russian attack on Kyiv in less than a week kills 20
items.description: President Volodymyr ⁠Zelenskyy urges NATO to take "strong decisions" on boosting Ukraine's air defences following the strike.

items.title: Suburban footballer dies after suffering head injury during game
items.description: Footy player and teacher Nathan Fitzgerald has died after suffering critical head injuries during a reserves game in the city's north on the weekend.

items.title: Highest ever pressure in Australia brings bitterly cold nights for south-east
items.description: Preliminary data shows the highest ever pressure in Australia was recorded in Tasmania on Monday morning.

items.title: Hamas to dissolve emergency government in Gaza
items.description: Hamas officials announced the resignation of senior members of the government, but warned that some people would remain in senior positions in Gaza's administration to "prevent any vacuum that could harm our citizens".

items.title: 'Assassination plot' impeachment trial involving Duterte dynasty begins in Manila
items.description: A highly consequential impeachment trial against Philippines Vice-President Sara Duterte could spell the end for her political career and shape the nation's 2028 election.

items.title: 'Like a small iceberg': Rare whale calf spotted swimming off east coast
items.description: The calf, thought to be one of only a dozen in the Southern Hemisphere, has been spotted swimming alongside its mother.

items.title: AFP confirms threat made against Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi
items.description: Australian Federal Police says a young person was identified and issued a formal warning over an online threat made towards Mr Modi, ahead of his official visit later this week.

items.title: PM apologises for saying he would 'shag' Kylie Minogue in podcast game
items.description: Anthony Albanese made the comments during a game of "shag, marry, date" on the Bush Deep podcast on Friday, which have been widely condemned as inappropriate.

items.title: This Place: Thaaklatjika Mingkana
items.description: Mutawintji National Park is an area rich in Aboriginal culture, painting and wildlife, and where the red desert is now green and lush. As part of NAIDOC Week the ABC is looking at Indigenous peoples' connection to country, and what makes it so special. NAIDOC Week is marking 50 years of Deadly and runs from July 5 until July 12.

items.title: Dozens killed and more than 100 injured in Sri Lanka prison riot
items.description: Victims with cuts and gunshot injuries have been rushed to hospital near the capital Colombo following the country's deadliest prison riot in years.

items.title: Three alleged escapes from custody in one month labelled 'major concern'
items.description: Police are searching for remand prisoner Isaac Thompson, 26, who they say is a "known associate" of the Mongols outlaw motorcycle gang, after he escaped custody during a medical transfer on Sunday night.

items.title: 'Oldest continually practised medicine' being passed on to students
items.description: Aboriginal Australians have used native plants as bush medicine for tens of thousands of years. On Larrakia land, medical students are learning how nature can heal.

items.title: 'I was feeling threatened': Men removed from Labor conference demand answers
items.description: As Premier Chris Minns walked into the Sydney Town Hall, greeting delegates ahead of his speech, two men unfurled a Palestinian flag from the second-floor balcony before being escorted from the event by police.

items.title: Love a self-saucing pudding? These four are delicious and easy
items.description: You'd never guess it but self-saucing puddings are so easy to make. Here are four of our best for you try while the weather is cool.

items.title: Is a full day of screen time for kids ever OK?
items.description: Screen time has become a phrase that makes "parents feel instantly guilty", but how detrimental is a full day of screens on the odd occasion, like during school holidays or when you are home sick?

items.title: 'Disgusting' antisemitic graffiti sprayed on Anzac landmark
items.description: Swastikas and anti-Jewish abuse were discovered spray-painted on rocks and the historic Plantagenet Battery along Western Australia's south coast.

items.title: 'Pink army' Thunderbirds fans flock to Rundle Mall
items.description: Hundreds of fans have flocked to Rundle Mall, dressed in pink, to welcome back the Adelaide Thunderbirds following an unforgettable grand final win.

items.title: Concerns about cricket pitches on ovals after Melbourne football tragedy
items.description: Nathan Fitzgerald's club has asked authorities to look at the way hard cricket pitches are covered on multi-use ovals as the 27-year-old continues to receive end-of-life care.

items.title: Ex-university chancellor fronts ICAC days after handing in resignation
items.description: Just days after resigning as chancellor at the University of Wollongong (UOW), Michael Still faces the state's corruption watchdog.
